_doc: Declared authority for every wp_ajax_* / wp_ajax_nopriv_* / admin_post_* /
admin_post_nopriv_* handler this plugin registers. AdminActionAuthorityTest walks the
live surface and fails when a handler is missing here, so a new admin action cannot
ship without someone stating who may fire it.
Why this surface needs its own manifest: every one of these is a state-changing
endpoint reachable by ANY logged-in user who knows the action name. There is no
permission_callback the way a REST route has one - the only thing between a member
and the mutation is whatever the callback body happens to check.
audience: admin = a capability holder | moderator = moderate_mvs_media |
member = any logged-in user, self-scoped | public = nopriv, anyone signed out.
capability: the literal cap string(s) the callback checks, '|' between alternatives,
or is_user_logged_in when logged-in IS the authority (which then needs a reason).
nonce_action: the action string passed to the nonce check; {param} marks a suffix
taken from the request, which is what makes the nonce per-object.
delegates_to: a named guard method that does the checking, declared here so the
delegation is a STATED FACT the test verifies, not something a reader infers.
get_reachable: the callback reads its object id from $_GET, so the action is
reachable by a followed link. Safe only because the nonce is per-object; recorded
so a future handler cannot quietly become GET-mutable without anyone noticing.
writes: every entry is true. Nothing on this surface is a read, so the test applies
its strictest rule everywhere and there is no wriggle room to claim otherwise.
A member or public entry MUST carry a reason. A nopriv handler MUST carry a reason.
Free registers 5 handlers. One (admin_post_mvs_report_status) is conditional: it
mounts only when Pro is absent, so it does not appear in a runtime walk on a site
running both. It carries conditional + conditional_on, the same escape hatch Pro's
route-authority.json uses for feature toggles.

admin_post_mvs_report_status.conditional_on: Plugin::init() registers admin.reports only when ! defined( 'MVS_PRO_VERSION' ) - Pro ships its own User Reports screen, and two reports menus would be confusing.
